Book Now Why PM Aesthetics Is The Best Choice For Your First Aesthetic Treatment If you're new to Botox, new to filler, new to laser treatments, or new to medical aesthetics entirely, PM Aesthetics is where you should start. ​ We specialize in first-time patients. The majority of our new patients have never had aesthetic treatments before, and they choose us because we prioritize education, safety, and realistic expectations over sales quotas and package pressure. ​ Here's why PM Aesthetics is the preferred choice in New Hampshire for patients new to aesthetics: 1. NO PROVIDER COMMISSIONS = NO SALES PRESSURE Our providers are not paid on commission.- This means you'll never be upsold treatments you don't need, pushed into packages you can't afford, or pressured to "decide today" for a discount. ​ What this means for new patients: You get honest recommendations based on what will actually work for YOUR face, YOUR goals, and YOUR budget, not what maximizes our revenue. Compare to: Most chain medspas and private equity-backed practices pay providers based on how much they sell. This creates inherent conflict between your best interest and their financial incentive. ​ Real example: You come in asking about lip filler. At a commission-based practice, you might be told you "need" 2 syringes ($1,400+), cheek filler ($800), jawline filler ($800), and a Botox lip flip ($150), total $3,150. ​ At PM Aesthetics,what is appropriate, that's what we recommend. We don't invent problems to sell solutions. 2. TRANSPARENT PRICING (NO HIDDEN COSTS, NO BAIT-AND-SWITCH) All pricing is published on our website. You know exactly what Botox costs per unit, what filler costs per syringe, what laser treatments cost per session, before you ever walk in the door. What this means for new patients: No surprises. No "consultation required" to learn basic pricing. No showing up expecting $300 and being told it's actually $1,200. Compare to: Most practices hide pricing behind "consultation required" or advertise artificially low "starting at" prices that don't reflect real treatment costs. Our transparent injectable pricing: NEUROTOXINS (Botox, Xeomin): - Botox: $15/unit - Xeomin: $13/unit DERMAL FILLERS: - All filler brands: $699/syringe 3. EDUCATION-FIRST APPROACH (WE EXPLAIN WHY, NOT JUST WHAT) We teach you about facial anatomy, aging processes, and how treatments actually work, not just "this is what we recommend." ​ What this means for new patients: You understand what you're getting, why it works, what realistic results look like, and how to maintain them. You leave educated, not just treated. Our educational resources for new patients: The Facial Aging Pyramid Comprehensive guide to how faces age (foundation, structure, surface, refinement) and why treating in order matters. Most practices skip foundation and go straight to fillers, we explain why that creates unnatural results. Lip Filler Guide What filler works where, how much you actually need (not how much they want to sell you), realistic expectations for each area. Treatment Timelines When you'll see results, how long they last, when to rebook. We don't tell you "lasts 6-12 months" we give you specific timelines based on product, area, and metabolism. ​ Pre- and Post-Treatment Protocols What to avoid before treatment (blood thinners, alcohol, NSAIDs), what to expect after (swelling, bruising timelines), how to optimize results. Compare to: Most practices provide minimal education, focusing on "you need this" rather than "here's why this works and what alternatives exist." Example of our educational approach: New patient asks about lip filler. Most practices: "We recommend 1-2 syringes of Juvéderm. That'll be $1,200-1,400. When would you like to schedule?" PM Aesthetics: "Let's talk about your goals. Are you looking for volume, definition, hydration, or symmetry correction? Here's how your lips age, where you've lost volume, and what we can realistically achieve. For your anatomy, I'd recommend starting with with a lip flip. We can always add more in your 2-week follow-up if needed. Here's what the recovery looks like, when you'll see final results, and how long it typically lasts. You'll also need to stay hydrated (80oz water daily) and use SPF to maintain results. Do you have questions about the process?" You leave understanding your face, not just buying a product. 4. CONSERVATIVE, NATURAL RESULTS (NOT INSTAGRAM FACE) We refuse overfilled lips, frozen foreheads, and unnatural results even if you request them. What this means for new patients: You won't walk out looking "done." You'll look like a refreshed, rested version of yourself. Most people won't know you had anything done, they'll just think you look great. Our treatment philosophy: Start conservatively: You can always add more in 2-week follow-up; you can't easily remove overfilled lips or over-Botoxed foreheads. Respect your anatomy: Not every face can or should have Kylie Jenner lips. We work with your natural bone structure, lip proportions, and facial balance, not against them. Prioritize longevity: Natural results age better than overdone ones. Overfilled faces look worse as you age; natural enhancement looks better over time. Say no when appropriate: If you request something that would look unnatural or age poorly, we'll tell you, and explain why. We'd rather lose a sale than deliver results you'll regret. Compare to: Many practices will give you whatever you ask for (and pay for), even if it looks bad. Their goal is transaction; ours is long-term relationship. 5. COMPREHENSIVE CONSULTATIONS (NOT RUSHED 15-MINUTE ASSESSMENTS) We spend 30-60 minutes in your first consultation** longer if needed, to assess your concerns, educate you on options, and create a personalized treatment plan. ​ What this means for new patients: You're not rushed. You get to ask every question. We explain everything until you're comfortable and informed. What we cover in first consultations: ​ Medical history review: Allergies, medications, previous treatments, contraindications Facial analysis: Bone structure, volume loss patterns, aging concerns, asymmetries Goal discussion: What bothers you most, what you want to achieve, what's realistic Treatment options: Multiple approaches, pros/cons of each, which we recommend and why Realistic expectations: What results look like, timeline, longevity, maintenance Pricing breakdown: Exact costs, payment options, membership benefits if applicable Alternative approaches: Sometimes lifestyle changes (SPF, sleep, hydration) matter more than treatments Compare to: Most practices do 10-15 minute "consultations" that are really sales pitches. You're told what you "need," given a price, and asked when you want to schedule. Why we charge a consultation fee: Our consultation fee is $100 (applied toward treatment if you book same day or within 2 weeks). For patients who prefer to start with no financial commitment, we offer free virtual consultations and complimentary in-person skin assessments before your first paid appointment. Why we charge it: It ensures you're serious and ready. We invest significant time and expertise in consultations, teaching facial anatomy, explaining treatment options, creating personalized plans. The fee ensures we're working with committed patients, not people comparing 8 practices for the lowest price. What you get for $100: 30-60 minute comprehensive assessment Personalized treatment plan Written recommendations and pricing Educational materials Direct provider time (not just front desk staff) $100 credit toward treatment if you book within 2 weeks Compare to: "Free consultations" at most practices are 10-minute sales pitches with high-pressure closing tactics. You're not getting education—you're getting sold. Our philosophy: We're here when you're ready. We don't chase, pressure, or discount to close same-day. We educate, recommend, and let you decide on your timeline. 6. REALISTIC EXPECTATIONS (WE TELL YOU WHAT WON'T WORK, NOT JUST WHAT WILL) We're more likely to talk you OUT of treatments than into them. ​ What this means for new patients: If a treatment won't achieve your goals, we tell you even if it means losing a sale. We'd rather you don't waste money than deliver disappointing results. Examples of realistic expectations we set: Botox for deep static wrinkles: "Botox prevents wrinkles from getting worse and reduces dynamic lines (ones that appear when you move your face). But for deep static wrinkles that are visible at rest, you'll also need resurfacing treatments (RF microneedling, laser) or filler. Botox alone won't erase them. Here's what improvement you can realistically expect..." Lip filler for chronically dehydrated lips: "Before we do filler, try drinking 80oz of water daily for 2 weeks. Dehydrated lips lose water 3-4x faster than facial skin. If you're dehydrated, filler will look worse and won't last as long. Let's address foundation first, then add volume if still needed." Laser hair removal for blonde/gray hair: "Laser hair removal works on dark hair with melanin. It won't work on blonde, red, gray, or white hair because there's no pigment for the laser to target. I don't want to take your money for treatments that won't work. Let's discuss alternatives like electrolysis." Fillers for significant sagging: "Filler can add volume, but it can't lift sagging skin. For jowls and significant laxity, you need Ultherapy (ultrasound lifting) or surgical options. Adding filler to sagging areas often makes it worse, creates heaviness and unnatural bulges. Here's what I actually recommend..." Compare to: Most practices will take your money for treatments that won't work, then blame your "anatomy" or "metabolism" when results disappoint. Our commitment: We only recommend treatments we believe will deliver meaningful improvement for your specific concerns. If we can't help, we tell you, and often refer you to specialists who can (dermatologists, plastic surgeons, therapists for body dysmorphia concerns). 7. NO PRESSURE OR FINANCING TRAPS We don't push financing. We don't create artificial urgency. What this means for new patients: You pay for what you need, when you need it. Our approach: Pay per treatment: Most patients prefer this. You try a treatment, see if you like results, decide if you want more. No commitment to packages you might not finish. Membership option (if it fits your goals): For patients who want ongoing treatments (monthly facials, regular Botox, consistent laser hair removal), membership provides savings. But we never pressure signup. No financing: We don't offer CareCredit. Why? Because financing makes it easy to overspend on treatments you can't afford. We'd rather you save up and pay cash than go into debt for aesthetics. Compare to: Most practices push packages heavily because it locks in revenue. Then you're stuck with prepaid treatments you might not want. Chain medspas aggressively push financing, making it easy to spend $5K+ without feeling the impact, until payments hit your budget for the next 2 years. Our philosophy: If you can't afford to pay cash for aesthetic treatments, you probably shouldn't be getting them yet. Focus on foundation (SPF, sleep, water, stress management) until you're financially ready for treatments. 8. EXPERIENCED PROVIDERS (NOT NEWLY TRAINED INJECTORS PRACTICING ON YOU) Our injectors have years of experience not months. You're not a training case. What this means for new patients: Your first injectable experience is with someone who's done thousands of treatments, understands anatomy deeply, and can handle complications if they arise. Compare to: Many chain medspas hire newly licensed nurses or aestheticians and have them start injecting immediately after basic training courses. You're literally their practice dummy. Some practices rotate providers constantly (whoever's working that day). You never see the same person twice, and they don't know your face or treatment history. Our commitment: You see the same provider(s) over time. They learn your face, remember what worked, adjust based on how you metabolize products. This continuity delivers better results. 9. MEDICAL OVERSIGHT & SAFETY PROTOCOLS We operate under medical oversight with strict safety protocols. What this means for new patients: Every treatment is performed according to medical best practices. We have emergency protocols if complications arise. We don't cut corners on safety to maximize profit. Our safety protocols: Medical history screening: We review allergies, medications, bleeding disorders, autoimmune conditions, pregnancy/breastfeeding status. If you're not a safe candidate, we don't treat, even if you want to proceed. Sterile technique: All injectables use sterile needles/cannulas, single-use supplies, proper skin prep. We never reuse needles or dilute products to stretch supply. Complication management: We stock hyaluronidase (filler reversal agent) on-site. If vascular occlusion occurs, we can dissolve filler immediately, potentially saving you from skin necrosis or blindness. Infection prevention: Proper post-treatment instructions, antibiotic protocols when indicated, monitoring for infections. Product authenticity: We only use FDA-approved products purchased directly from manufacturers (Allergan & Merz). Never black-market fillers, never counterfeit Botox, never expired products. Compare to: Some practices (especially unlicensed "med spas") cut corners on safety, reusing needles, using counterfeit products, treating high-risk patients, having no complication protocols. The "deal" you get at an unlicensed practice could cost you your vision or result in disfiguring complications. Our commitment: Safety first, always. We'd rather turn away a patient than take unnecessary risk. 10. HONEST ABOUT WHAT WE DON'T OFFER (AND WHO CAN HELP YOU INSTEAD) We don't try to be everything to everyone. If we don't offer a treatment you need, we tell you, and refer you to someone who does. Treatments we DON'T offer (and where to go instead): Surgical facelifts, blepharoplasty, rhinoplasty: Refer to: Board-certified plastic surgeons in Boston/NH Aggressive ablative lasers (CO2, Erbium): Refer to: Dermatologists with surgical laser expertise NOTE: CO2 Laser is inappropriate for a medspa setting. Body contouring beyond Venus Bliss: Refer to: surgical liposuction Hair transplants: Refer to: Hair restoration surgeons Permanent makeup, microblading: Refer to: Licensed permanent makeup artists Thread lifts: We don't offer these because evidence shows poor outcomes, high complication rates, and temporary results that don't justify cost/risk. Compare to: Many practices will offer treatments they're not qualified for (unlicensed people doing injectables, aestheticians doing medical procedures) or recommend treatments that don't work just to make the sale. Our philosophy: We'd rather lose a sale and maintain our integrity than offer subpar treatments or operate outside our scope. Here, they taught me about my face and options. Worth every penny." "Medicine-first approach matters." "This isn't a chain medspa trying to hit sales quotas. It's a medical practice that happens to offer aesthetic treatments. That distinction matters." Common Questions From New Patients "I've never had Botox before. How do I know if I need it?" You're a good candidate for Botox if: You have dynamic wrinkles (lines that appear when you make expressions, forehead lines, crow's feet, frown lines between eyebrows) You want to prevent those lines from becoming permanent static wrinkles You're bothered by the appearance of these lines You're NOT a good candidate for Botox if: Your primary concern is static wrinkles (visible at rest), you need resurfacing or filler You have certain medical conditions (myasthenia gravis, ALS, neuromuscular disorders) You're pregnant or breastfeeding You want completely frozen results (we don't do that) What to expect: First time: We start conservatively (typically 20-40 units depending on areas treated) Results: Visible in 3-5 days, peak at 2 weeks, last 3-4 months Follow-up: We see you at 2 weeks to assess and add more if needed Maintenance: Most patients rebook every 3-4 months "I want lip filler but I'm terrified of duck lips. How do I avoid that?" Our approach to natural lip enhancement: Respect your proportions: Your upper and lower lip should maintain natural ratio (usually 1:1.6 or 1:2). We don't create disproportionate "top-heavy" or "bottom-heavy" lips. ​ Strategic placement matters: We place filler in specific locations to enhance your natural shape not just "pump volume everywhere." This creates definition without overfilled appearance. 2-week assessment: We see you at 2 weeks to assess. If you want more volume, we can add. If you're happy, we're done. Building gradually prevents overdoing it. What to avoid: Overfilling (obvious duck lips) Ignoring proportions (creating unnatural ratios) "Shelf" appearance (filler migration above lip line) "Sausage lips" (horizontal lines of filler with no definition) "How do I know how much Botox I need?" Typical first-time dosing: Forehead lines: 10-20 units (depends on muscle strength, how much movement you want to preserve) Frown lines (11s between eyebrows): 20-25 units (most people need full dose here underdosing doesn't work) Crow's feet (both sides): 12-24 units (6-12 units per side) Full "Botox 3" (forehead + frown + crow's feet): 40-64 units total Additional areas: Lip flip: 4-6 units Bunny lines (nose): 4-6 units Gummy smile: 2-4 units per side Masseter (jaw slimming/TMJ): 60-100 units total (30-50 per side) Why dosing varies: Muscle strength (stronger muscles need more units) Gender (men typically need 20-40% more than women) Desired result (full freeze vs. softening with movement) Metabolism (some people metabolize faster, need higher doses) Our approach: We start conservatively for first-timers, assess at 2 weeks, adjust dose for future treatments based on your response. "What's the difference between Botox and Xeomin? Which should I choose?" All three are neurotoxins that work the same way (block signals from nerves to muscles, preventing contraction). Differences are subtle: BOTOX (onabotulinumtoxinA): Onset: 3-5 days Peak: 10-14 days Duration: 3-4 months average Diffusion: Low (stays localized) Best for: Precise areas (crow's feet, lip flip, precise forehead work) Cost: $15/unit XEOMIN (incobotulinumtoxinA): Onset: 2-5 days Peak: 10-14 days Duration: 3-4 months Diffusion: Similar to Botox Unique feature: No accessory proteins (lower antibody formation risk) Best for: Patients who've developed resistance to Botox/Dysport, large-area treatments (masseter, forehead) Cost: $13/unit (slightly less than Botox/Dysport) Which we recommend: First-time patients: Botox or Xeomin (predictable, precise) Large areas (forehead, masseter): Xeomin (cost-effective) Developed resistance to other toxins: Xeomin Honest truth: For most patients, differences are minimal. Price and provider experience matter more than product choice. "I'm new to laser hair removal. How many sessions will I need?" Realistic timeline for laser hair removal: Typical treatment series: 6-8 sessions spaced 4-8 weeks apart (depending on area and hair growth cycle) Why multiple sessions: Hair grows in cycles (anagen, catagen, telogen). Laser only works on hair in active growth phase (anagen). Since only 20-30% of hair is in anagen at any time, you need multiple treatments to catch all follicles in growth phase. Expected results: After 3 sessions: 30-40% reduction After 6 sessions: 70-85% reduction After 8 sessions: 85-95% reduction Maintenance: Most patients need 1-2 touch-up sessions per year after initial series to maintain results. What determines number of sessions: Hair color (dark hair responds best, blonde/red/gray won't respond) Skin color (lighter skin = easier to treat safely, darker skin requires more conservative settings) Area (face responds faster than body; hormonal areas like chin/bikini may need more sessions) Hormonal factors (PCOS, hormonal imbalances may require ongoing maintenance) "What should I do before my first Botox appointment?" 7-10 days before treatment, avoid: Blood thinners (aspirin, ibuprofen, naproxen, fish oil, vitamin E, turmeric)—increases bruising risk Alcohol (3+ drinks)—vasodilator, increases bruising Intense exercise 24 hours before—increases blood flow, slight bruising risk increase Day of treatment: Arrive with clean face (no makeup if possible) Eat normally (don't come on empty stomach—can increase dizziness risk) Communicate concerns (if nervous, tell us—we'll go slower, explain more) After treatment (24-48 hours): Avoid: Lying flat for 4 hours (can cause product migration) Intense exercise for 24 hours Facials, massage, or manipulating injection sites for 24 hours Alcohol for 24 hours Heat exposure (saunas, hot yoga) for 24-48 hours Expect: Mild redness at injection sites (resolves in 30-60 minutes) Possible small bumps (resolve in 1-2 hours) Rare bruising (5-10% of patients) No visible results immediately (takes 3-5 days) Follow-up: We see you at 2 weeks to assess results and make any adjustments (included in initial cost). "What's the consultation fee and why do you charge it?" Our consultation fee is $100 (applied toward treatment if you book same day or within 2 weeks). Why we charge a consultation fee: ​ 1. Time investment: Comprehensive first consultations take 30-60 minutes. We're assessing your concerns, educating you on facial anatomy, explaining treatment options, discussing realistic expectations, answering questions. 2. Provider expertise: You're getting direct time with experienced medical providers, not just front desk staff doing sales pitches. 3. Ensures serious inquiries: Free consultations attract price-shoppers who book 8 practices and choose the cheapest. We'd rather work with patients who value education and expertise over lowest price. 4. Reduces no-shows: When consultations are free, 30-40% of people don't show up. Paid consultations have 95%+ show rates because patients are invested. 5. Applied toward treatment: If you book treatment same day or within 2 weeks, the $100 is credited toward your treatment cost. You're essentially prepaying $100 of your first treatment. What "free consultations" actually cost you: Most practices offer free consultations, but: They're 10-15 minutes max (rushed sales pitch, not education) High-pressure closing tactics ("book today and save 20%") Bait-and-switch pricing (advertise low "starting at" prices, actual cost is 3-4x higher) Commission-driven recommendations (you're sold what maximizes their revenue, not what you need) You pay more in the long run through unnecessary treatments, overpriced packages, or disappointing results from rushed decisions. Our philosophy: We're here when you're ready. The $100 consultation fee ensures we're working with patients who value education and are prepared to make informed decisions, not impulse buyers chasing the cheapest option. What to Expect at Your First Appointment Step 1: Medical History & Intake (10 minutes) Review medical history, medications, allergies Discuss previous aesthetic treatments (if any) Document concerns, goals, expectations Step 2: Facial Analysis (10-15 minutes) Assess facial anatomy, bone structure, volume loss Identify aging patterns (how YOUR face ages) Note asymmetries, proportions, areas of concern Take photos (for your records and treatment planning) Step 3: Education & Treatment Options (15-20 minutes) Explain why your concerns exist (aging process, anatomy, lifestyle factors) Discuss treatment options (what addresses your specific concerns) Explain how treatments work, realistic expectations, timelines Show before/after examples of similar cases Step 4: Personalized Treatment Plan (10-15 minutes) Recommend specific treatments in order of priority Explain why we're recommending this sequence Provide pricing breakdown Discuss timeline (when to start, spacing between treatments, maintenance) Step 5: Q&A & Decision Time (As long as needed) Answer every question you have Clarify anything confusing Provide written treatment plan and pricing No pressure to decide today take time to think If you decide to proceed same day: Review and sign consent forms Provide pre-treatment instructions Perform treatment Provide post-treatment instructions Schedule follow-up appointment If you want to think about it: Take home written treatment plan Call or email with additional questions Schedule treatment when ready (consultation fee credit valid for 2 weeks) Total time: 45-90 minutes depending on complexity of concerns and number of questions. View Our Services Getting Married? Start Here. Your wedding day results depend almost entirely on when you start. Most brides begin too late for the treatments that make the biggest difference. The treatments that lift, tighten, and remodel, Ultherapy, TriLift, RF Microneedling, require months to develop fully. Botox and filler need time to settle and be adjusted before your day. Even surface treatments like chemical peels have optimal timing windows for photos. Here's the short version of what the timeline looks like: 12 months out — Ultherapy, TriLift, foundational lifting and collagen remodeling. Start now if your wedding is this fall. 6 months out — RF Microneedling series, IPL, dermal filler. Results need time to build and settle. 3 months out — Botox, Xeomin, lip filler. Especially critical for first-time patients who need adjustment time. 6 weeks out — VI Peel, DiamondGlow, SaltFacial. Skin at its clearest for photos. 2 weeks out — Toxin touch-up only. Nothing new or unfamiliar this close to the date. Wedding week — Nothing new. You're ready.
